products.name: Turnitin AI Detection
products.note: AI writing detection; academic integrity; false positive risk; student data privacy (FERPA)

reading.body:
Turnitin's AI detection tool addresses a real constraint in education: distinguishing student work from AI-generated text, but the company's data reveals significant blind spots around accuracy and privacy that limit its reliability as an integrity measure.

The company positions AI Detection as a solution to academic integrity by identifying when students use generative AI to write assignments. The tool integrates into learning management systems and covers diverse document types from essays to dissertations. This approach assumes detection accuracy is feasible and sufficient to solve the underlying problem of verifying authorship at scale across education institutions.

The data flags two critical gaps. False positive risk means the tool will flag human writing as AI-generated, creating harm without evidence of actual wrongdoing. Student data privacy under FERPA means institutions using this tool must handle sensitive educational records, but the data does not cover what happens to that data, how long it is retained, or who can access it. These are not edge cases but core operational risks for any detection system applied to minors and protected educational records.

The data does not indicate whether Turnitin's detection improves over time, how institutions should handle false positives, or whether the tool addresses the upstream question of why students resort to AI writing in the first place. It measures a symptom rather than the constraint it claims to solve.

profile_text.body:
Turnitin is an education technology company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Oakland. According to its website, its solutions promote academic integrity, streamline grading and feedback, deter plagiarism, and improve student outcomes. The company describes its focus as helping institutions guide responsible AI use and assess student work securely.

Its tracked product is Turnitin AI Detection, which the company describes as identifying AI-generated writing, comparing student work against what it calls the world's largest academic database, and operating inside a learning management system. The site also describes writing analytics and AI insights, and separate tools for secure exams that lock down devices to block the internet, integrated AI tools, and notes, verify student identity, and deliver digital exams offline. A further offering scans documents, grant proposals, theses, and dissertations for text similarity and AI writing. Turnitin states that it uses AI selectively to create marketing materials, with that content reviewed, edited, and fact-checked by humans.

The product record notes two concerns attached to AI writing detection: false positive risk and student data privacy under FERPA. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
